title: Understanding Convergence Diagnostics
text: running APS, know search converged? raw --sample correlation 0.6 mean: Bad surrogate: model underfitting; iterations help Noisy surface: simulation high Monte Carlo noise; model can better APS provides diagnostics distinguish cases.

title: Understanding Convergence Diagnostics
text: key insight Monte Carlo noise creates ceiling achievable correlation. simulation y=m(𝐱)+εy = m(\mathbf{x}) + \varepsilon : - m(𝐱)m(\mathbf{x}) true response surface - ε\varepsilon MC noise variance σ2\sigma^2 - Signal variance τ2=Var(m(𝐱))\tau^2 = \text{Var}(m(\mathbf{x})) even perfect surrogate achieves : ρ*=ττ2+σ2\rho^* = \frac{\tau}{\sqrt{\tau^2 + \sigma^2}} reliability ratio normalizes observed correlation ceiling: ρ̃=ρoutρ*\tilde{\rho} = \frac{\rho_{\text{}}}{\rho^*} ρ̃≈1\tilde{\rho} \approx 1: Surrogate learned learnable signal ρ̃≪1\tilde{\rho} \ll 1: Room improvement

title: Understanding Convergence Diagnostics
text: Output:
code: library(aps)  # Run APS result <- aps(   obj_function = my_simulation,   n_params = 3,   n_iter = 10,   n_obs = 100 )  # Get the diagnostic diag <- reliability_ratio(result) print(diag) APS Convergence Diagnostic: Reliability Ratio ==============================================  Sample size: 1100 points Nearest neighbors used: k = 1  Variance Decomposition:   Total variance (Var(y)):  2.4500   Noise variance (sigma^2): 0.3200   Signal variance (tau^2):  2.1300   Signal-to-noise ratio:    6.66  Correlation Diagnostic:   Maximum achievable (rho*):   0.932   Observed out-of-sample:      0.891   Reliability ratio (rho~):    0.956  Interpretation:   Excellent (rho_tilde = 0.96). The surrogate has extracted nearly all   learnable signal. Continued optimization is unlikely to find   substantially better regions.

title: Understanding Convergence Diagnostics
text: plot shows: Circles: -sample correlation (training fit) Squares: --sample correlation (predictive ability) Arrows: Change -sample --sample Green dashed lines: Per-iteration ρ*\rho^* (ceiling)
code: plot(result, type = "correlation")

title: Understanding Convergence Diagnostics
text: Good convergence: - --sample correlations (squares) near green line - Stable across iterations Overfitting: - Large gaps circles squares - -sample high, --sample low Underfitting: - -sample --sample well green line - May need data different architectures

title: Understanding Convergence Diagnostics
text: green segments can vary across iterations. happens : Heteroskedastic noise: Different regions different noise levels Exploitation focusing: Later iterations sample noisier regions near minimum
code: # Example with location-dependent noise hetero_fn <- function(x) {   signal <- sum(x^2)   # Noise is HIGH near the minimum, LOW in corners   local_sigma <- 0.3 + 2 * exp(-signal)   signal + rnorm(1, sd = local_sigma) }  result <- aps(   obj_function = hetero_fn,   n_params = 2,   x_min = -2, x_max = 2,   n_iter = 5,   n_obs = 80 )  plot(result, type = "correlation") # Green segments will be LOWER for later iterations # (which focus on the noisy minimum region)

title: Understanding Convergence Diagnostics
text: APS estimates σ2\sigma^2 using nearest-neighbor differences: σ̂2=12n∑=1n(yi−ynn())2\hat{\sigma}^2 = \frac{1}{2n} \sum_{=1}^{n} (y_i - y_{nn()})^2 works nearby points similar signal, differencing isolates noise. can adjust number neighbors:
code: # Use k=3 neighbors for smoother estimate (more bias, less variance) diag <- reliability_ratio(result, k = 3)  # Also works in plots plot(result, type = "correlation", k = 3)

title: Understanding Convergence Diagnostics
text: Use reliability ratio automatic stopping: stopping condition requires : 1. ρ̃≥\tilde{\rho} \geq threshold (surrogate good) 2. Minimum hasn’t improved N iterations (nothing better find)
code: result <- aps(   obj_function = my_simulation,   n_params = 5,   n_iter = 50,  # Maximum iterations   n_obs = 100,   early_stop = TRUE,   rho_tilde_threshold = 0.95,  # Stop when 95% of signal learned  min_stable_iters = 2          # AND minimum stable for 2 iterations )  # Check if stopped early result$stopped_early result$final_iteration

title: Understanding Convergence Diagnostics
text: diagnostic also reports SNR = τ2/σ2\tau^2 / \sigma^2: SNR > 10: Strong signal, noise minor SNR ≈ 1: Signal noise comparable SNR < 1: Noise dominates; may need replications per evaluation
code: diag <- reliability_ratio(result) diag$snr  # If SNR is very low, consider: # 1. Increasing replications within your simulation # 2. Using variance reduction techniques # 3. Accepting that this surface is inherently noisy

title: Getting Started with APS
text: Adversarial Parameter Selection (APS) R package finding parameter configurations expose worst-case performance Monte Carlo simulations. uses Bayesian optimization deep ensembles efficiently search parameter space. Key use case: simulation study comparing statistical methods. Instead testing fixed grid parameters, APS actively searches parameters methods perform worst.

title: Getting Started with APS
code: # Install from GitHub devtools::install_github("AustinJang/aps")  # torch is required - install if needed install.packages("torch") torch::install_torch()

title: Getting Started with APS
text: Define objective function takes parameter vector returns performance statistic (lower = worse):
code: library(aps)  # Simple example: find where an estimator has highest bias obj_fn <- function(x) {   # Simulate: x[1] = effect size, x[2] = noise level   set.seed(42)  # For reproducibility within each call   y <- rnorm(100, mean = x[1], sd = x[2])    # Performance metric: negative absolute bias (lower = worse)   -abs(mean(y) - x[1]) }  # Run APS result <- aps(   obj_function = obj_fn,   n_params = 2,   x_min = c(0, 0.1),   x_max = c(1, 2),   n_iter = 5,   n_obs = 100 )  # View results print(result) summary(result)

title: Getting Started with APS
text: result object contains: best_x: Parameter values producing worst (lowest) performance best_y: worst performance value found x, y: evaluated parameter values performance architecture_df: Model performance across iterations
code: # Best adversarial point result$best_x result$best_y  # How many evaluations total? nrow(result$x)  # Performance by iteration tapply(result$y, result$iteration, min)

title: Getting Started with APS
text: APS provides two diagnostic plots (requires ggplot2): correlation plot shows: - Circles: -sample correlation (training fit) - Squares: --sample correlation (predictive quality) - Green dashed line: rho* (maximum achievable given noise)
code: # Performance over iterations plot(result, type = "performance")  # Model correlation with noise-adjusted ceiling plot(result, type = "correlation")

title: Getting Started with APS
text: Enable automatic stopping surrogate learned learnable signal:
code: result <- aps(   obj_function = obj_fn,   n_params = 2,   n_iter = 20,   n_obs = 100,   early_stop = TRUE,   rho_tilde_threshold = 0.95,   min_stable_iters = 2 )  # Did it stop early? result$stopped_early result$final_iteration

title: Getting Started with APS
text: long runs, save progress iteration:
code: result <- aps(   obj_function = expensive_simulation,   n_params = 5,   n_iter = 50,   checkpoint_file = "aps_checkpoint.rds" )  # Resume if interrupted result <- aps(   obj_function = expensive_simulation,   n_params = 5,   n_iter = 50,   resume_from = "aps_checkpoint.rds" )

title: Vector Mode and Deferred Scalarization
text: Real simulations return multiple statistics: bias method , bias method B, RMSE, coverage, etc. running expensive search, often want ask different question: “fail?” → “fail relative B?” “Maximize RMSE” → “Maximize coverage gap” scalar mode, ’d re-run everything. Vector mode solves .

title: Vector Mode and Deferred Scalarization
text: Instead returning scalar, objective function returns named vector:
code: library(aps)  # Returns a vector of metrics obj_fn <- function(x) {   # Simulate data   set.seed(42)   y <- rnorm(100, mean = x[1], sd = x[2])    c(     bias_mean = mean(y) - x[1],     bias_median = median(y) - x[1],     rmse_mean = sqrt(mean((y - x[1])^2)),     coverage = mean(abs(y - x[1]) < 1.96 * x[2])   ) }  # The reduction function maps vector → scalar # APS minimizes this scalar result <- aps(   obj_function = obj_fn,   n_params = 2,   x_min = c(0, 0.1),   x_max = c(1, 2),   n_iter = 5,   n_obs = 100,   reduction = function(v) -abs(v["bias_mean"])  # Minimize negative bias )

title: Vector Mode and Deferred Scalarization
text: magic: APS stores full vector every point. Change question without re-running:
code: # Original question: where is bias_mean worst? result$best_y result$best_x  # New question: where is coverage lowest? result_coverage <- rereduce(result, function(v) v["coverage"]) result_coverage$best_y result_coverage$best_x  # Another question: where does mean beat median? result_gap <- rereduce(result, function(v) {   abs(v["bias_mean"]) - abs(v["bias_median"])  # Positive = mean worse }) result_gap$best_y result_gap$best_x

title: Vector Mode and Deferred Scalarization
text: full output matrix stored y_raw:
code: # Raw outputs: rows = evaluations, columns = output components dim(result$y_raw) colnames(result$y_raw)  # Extract all coverage values result$y_raw[, "coverage"]  # Find which parameters gave coverage < 0.9 low_coverage_idx <- which(result$y_raw[, "coverage"] < 0.9) result$x[low_coverage_idx, ]

title: Vector Mode and Deferred Scalarization
text: typical use case: comparing estimators across effect trajectories.
code: # Objective returns per-estimator RMSE did_sim <- function(alpha) {   # alpha is a 5-element effect trajectory   # ... run simulation ...    c(     twfe_rmse = 0.5,      # Placeholder values     csa_rmse = 0.3,     gardner_rmse = 0.4,     ascm_rmse = 0.2   ) }  # Find where ANY estimator fails result <- aps(   obj_function = did_sim,   n_params = 5,   x_min = -1, x_max = 1,   n_iter = 10,   n_obs = 50,   reduction = function(v) -max(v)  # Worst across all estimators )  # Post-hoc: where does TWFE specifically fail? result_twfe <- rereduce(result, function(v) -v["twfe_rmse"])  # Where is the gap between TWFE and ASCM largest? result_gap <- rereduce(result, function(v) {   v["twfe_rmse"] - v["ascm_rmse"]  # Positive = TWFE worse })

title: Vector Mode and Deferred Scalarization
text: can resume existing run new reduction function:
code: # Original run result1 <- aps(   obj_function = obj_fn,   n_params = 2,   n_iter = 5,   reduction = function(v) -v["bias_mean"],   checkpoint_file = "checkpoint.rds" )  # Resume with different reduction - no re-simulation! # Stored y_raw is re-scalarized with new reduction result2 <- aps(   obj_function = obj_fn,   n_params = 2,   n_iter = 10,   reduction = function(v) -v["coverage"],  # New question   resume_from = "checkpoint.rds" )

title: Vector Mode and Deferred Scalarization
text: summary function shows statistics output component:
code: summary(result) # Output mode: vector (4 components) # Output names: bias_mean, bias_median, rmse_mean, coverage # # Raw Output Statistics (across all evaluations): #   bias_mean: min=-0.12, mean=0.01, max=0.15 #   ... # # Reduced Performance Statistics: #   Min (adversarial): -0.12 #   ...

title: Vector Mode and Deferred Scalarization
text: Store , ask many questions: expensive simulation runs ; reductions cheap Named vectors: Use names clarity reference outputs reduction functions rereduce() instant: simulation, just re-computes y y_raw Resume preserves y_raw: Even resuming new reduction

title: Adversarial Parameter Selection for Monte Carlo Simulations
text: R package adversarial parameter selection Monte Carlo simulation studies. Uses Bayesian optimization deep ensembles identify parameter configurations expose worst-case method performance.

title: Adversarial Parameter Selection for Monte Carlo Simulations
code: # Install from GitHub devtools::install_github("AustinJang/aps")  # torch is required - install if needed install.packages("torch") torch::install_torch()

title: Adversarial Parameter Selection for Monte Carlo Simulations
code: library(aps)  # Define an objective function that takes a parameter vector # and returns a performance statistic (lower = worse) obj_fn <- function(x) {   # Example: compare two estimators on simulated data   # x[1] = effect size, x[2] = noise level   set.seed(42)   y <- rnorm(100, mean = x[1], sd = x[2])    # Performance: absolute bias of mean estimator   abs(mean(y) - x[1]) }  # Run adversarial parameter selection result <- aps(    obj_function = obj_fn,   n_params = 2,   x_min = c(0, 0.1),   x_max = c(1, 2),   n_iter = 5,   n_obs = 100 )  # View results print(result) summary(result)  # Diagnostic plots (requires ggplot2) plot(result, type = "performance") plot(result, type = "correlation")
